target.title: fix(agents): handle ripgrep stdout/stderr stream errors in grep tool
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The built-in grep tool owned a piped ripgrep child but did not handle stdout or stderr stream failures. Node treats an unhandled `error` event as process-fatal, and readline removes its input-error listener when the interface closes, so a pipe failure could crash the agent runtime or escape after cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

One lifecycle-owned stream-error helper now terminates ripgrep, closes readline, removes the abort listener, and rejects the tool promise exactly once. Both readline's re-emitted input error and the direct stdout guard remain attached; the direct guard is required after readline closes. The implementation mirrors the landed find-tool invariant without adding a new shared abstraction.

Duplicate proof scaffolding and the root changelog edit were removed. Test kill state is modeled without mutating Node's readonly child-process property.

## User Impact

Grep tool calls fail with a contextual stdout/stderr error instead of crashing the Gateway, hanging, or returning incomplete matches.

## Evidence

- Current head `612a686a5c18d31abfd5811e6c21fe9255cfd807`; focused head `66d6b728a001f23075bf82ff6e8244d09c7e7c3d` on sanitized public-network AWS Crabbox `cbx_81807643f51a` with no Tailscale or instance profile:
  - run `run_f0ff41fe6048`: `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.stream-errors.test.ts` — 3/3 passed.
  - run `run_678bc00cab3e`: real managed ripgrep searched a fixture successfully, then real stdout and stderr pipe failures terminated their children while the parent stayed alive.
- Fresh Codex AutoReview: clean, confidence 0.83.
- Current runtime/test blobs match the live-proven blobs after the base-only rebase.
- Exact-head hosted CI is running on the post-QA-fix base.

The stream contract was checked against Node's official EventEmitter documentation and readline implementation.
